cor-flow-solvable.title: Solvable flow problems
cor-flow-solvable.html: Let N∈Mm×k(R) be the incidence matrix of a connected network, and let s∈Rm. Then Nf=s has a solution if and only if s1+⋯+sm=0. In that case the solutions form f0+nul(N) for any one solution f0, and dim⁡nul(N)=k−m+1.

cor-more-unknowns-than-equations.title: More unknowns than equations
cor-more-unknowns-than-equations.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) with n>m.

  1. The homogeneous system Ax=0 has a non-trivial solution.
  2. Consequently, every list of n vectors in Fm with n>m is linearly dependent.

cor-pivot-columns-well-defined.title: Pivot columns are well defined
cor-pivot-columns-well-defined.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) have columns a1,…,an. Define the pivot columns of A to be the pivot columns of the RREF of A.

  1. Column l is a pivot column of A if and only if al∉span(a1,…,al−1).
  2. If E is any matrix in row echelon form that is row equivalent to A, then the pivot columns of E are the pivot columns of A. In particular, every row echelon form of A has the same number of non-zero rows.

cor-rank-from-any-echelon-form.title: Rank from any echelon form
cor-rank-from-any-echelon-form.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F), and let G be a matrix in row echelon form that is row equivalent to A. Then the number of non-zero rows of G is rankA, and the columns of G containing its pivots are exactly the pivot columns of A.

cor-unique-solution-iff-trivial-kernel.title: Uniqueness of solutions
cor-unique-solution-iff-trivial-kernel.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) have columns a1,…,an, and let b∈Fm be such that Ax=b is consistent. The following are equivalent:

  1. Ax=b has exactly one solution;
  2. Ax=0 has only the trivial solution;
  3. the list (a1,…,an) is linearly independent.

def-column-space.title: Column space
def-column-space.html: The column space of A∈Mm×n(F) is the span of its columns, col(A):=span(a1,…,an)={Ax:x∈Fn}⊆Fm.

def-elementary-matrix.title: Elementary matrix
def-elementary-matrix.html:
Let m≥1. A matrix E∈Mm(F) is an elementary matrix if it is obtained from Im by performing exactly one elementary row operation. Writing Eij for the matrix unit (1 in entry (i,j), 0 elsewhere; see @exm-standard-bases), the three kinds are:

  1. Pij, obtained by Ri↔Rj with i≠j: the identity with rows i and j swapped;
  2. Di(c)=diag(1,…,1,c,1,…,1), with c in position i, obtained by Ri→cRi with c≠0;
  3. Im+cEij, obtained by Ri→Ri+cRj with i≠j and c∈F: the identity with an extra c in entry (i,j).

def-elementary-row-operations.title: Elementary row operations
def-elementary-row-operations.html:
Let F be a field and let M∈Mm×k(F) have rows r1,…,rm. An elementary row operation on M is one of the following.

  1. Swap two rows: for i≠j, exchange ri and rj. Notation: Ri↔Rj.
  2. Scale a row: for an index i and a scalar c∈F with c≠0, replace ri by cri. Notation: Ri→cRi.
  3. Replace a row by adding a multiple of another row: for indices i≠j and any c∈F, replace ri by ri+crj. Notation: Ri→Ri+cRj.

In each case the rows not mentioned are left unchanged.

def-homogeneous-system.title: Homogeneous system
def-homogeneous-system.html: A linear system Ax=b over F is homogeneous if b=0. The vector 0∈Fn is a solution of every homogeneous system Ax=0, called the trivial solution. For any system Ax=b, the system Ax=0, with the same coefficient matrix, is its associated homogeneous system.

def-incidence-matrix.title: Incidence matrix
def-incidence-matrix.html: The incidence matrix of a network with vertices 1,…,m and edges 1,…,k, where k≥1, is N∈Mm×k(R) with Nve={1if v=tail(e),−1if v=head(e),0otherwise.

def-linear-system.title: Linear system
def-linear-system.html:
Let F be a field and let m,n≥1. A system of m linear equations in n unknowns x1,…,xn over F is a list of equations a11x1+a12x2+⋯+a1nxn=b1,a21x1+a22x2+⋯+a2nxn=b2,  ⋮am1x1+am2x2+⋯+amnxn=bm, where all aij and bi lie in F.

  • The coefficient matrix is A=(aij)∈Mm×n(F), the right-hand side is b=(b1,…,bm)∈Fm, and the system is written Ax=b.
  • The augmented matrix is the m×(n+1) matrix [A∣b] obtained by appending b to A as a last column.
  • A solution is a vector s=(s1,…,sn)∈Fn such that every equation holds when xj=sj for all j; equivalently, As=b. The solution set is the set of all solutions, a subset of Fn.
  • The system is consistent if it has at least one solution, and inconsistent if its solution set is empty.

def-lu-factorization.title: LU factorization
def-lu-factorization.html: A matrix L∈Mn(F) is unit lower triangular if it is lower triangular and every diagonal entry equals 1. Let A∈Mn(F). An LU factorization of A is a pair (L,U) of matrices in Mn(F) such that A=LU,L is **unit** lower triangular,U is upper triangular.

def-null-space.title: Null space
def-null-space.html: The null space of A∈Mm×n(F) is the solution set of the homogeneous system, nul(A):={x∈Fn:Ax=0}⊆Fn.

def-nullity-matrix.title: Nullity of a matrix
def-nullity-matrix.html: The nullity of A∈Mm×n(F) is nullityA:=dim⁡nul(A).

def-permutation-matrix.title: Permutation matrix
def-permutation-matrix.html: Let σ∈Sn be a permutation of {1,…,n}. The permutation matrix of σ is Pσ=(eσ(1)eσ(2)⋯eσ(n))∈Mn(F), the matrix whose j-th column is eσ(j). A matrix is a permutation matrix if it equals Pσ for some σ∈Sn.

def-plu-factorization.title: PLU factorization
def-plu-factorization.html: Let A∈Mn(F). A PLU factorization of A is a triple (P,L,U) of matrices in Mn(F) such that PA=LU,P is a permutation matrix,L is unit lower triangular,U is upper triangular.

def-rank-matrix.title: Rank of a matrix
def-rank-matrix.html: The rank of A∈Mm×n(F) is rankA:=dim⁡col(A).

def-reduced-row-echelon-form.title: Reduced row echelon form
def-reduced-row-echelon-form.html:
A matrix R∈Mm×k(F) is in reduced row echelon form (RREF) if it is in row echelon form, with pivot columns j1<⋯<jr, and moreover:

  1. every pivot equals 1: riji=1 for i=1,…,r; and
  2. every pivot is the only non-zero entry in its column: rhji=0 for all h≠i.

def-row-echelon-form.title: Row echelon form
def-row-echelon-form.html:
A matrix R∈Mm×k(F) is in row echelon form if:

  1. there is an integer r with 0≤r≤m such that rows 1,…,r are non-zero and rows r+1,…,m are zero; and
  2. if the leading entry of row i lies in column ji, for i=1,…,r, then j1<j2<⋯<jr, strictly.

The leading entries of rows 1,…,r are the pivots of R, and the columns j1,…,jr are its pivot columns.

def-row-equivalent.title: Row equivalence
def-row-equivalent.html: Let A,B∈Mm×k(F). We say A is row equivalent to B if B can be obtained from A by a finite sequence of elementary row operations. The empty sequence is allowed, so every matrix is row equivalent to itself.

def-row-space.title: Row space
def-row-space.html: The row space of A∈Mm×n(F) is the span of its rows, row(A):=span(row 1,…,row m)⊆M1×n(F).

exm-balance-ammonia.title: Burning ammonia
exm-balance-ammonia.html: Find all solutions of the system above over Q, and hence the balanced equation with the smallest positive integer coefficients.

exm-bases-of-three-subspaces.title: Bases for the running example
exm-bases-of-three-subspaces.html: Find bases of col(A), row(A) and nul(A), and the rank and nullity, for A=(1200−1241001211200113)∈M4×5(R).

exm-echelon-forms.html: Decide which of the following real matrices are in row echelon form, and which are in reduced row echelon form. Give the pivot columns where they exist. P=(21300−1000),Q=(15020013),T=(102001010),Z=(0000).

exm-elementary-matrices.html: Let A=(120134)∈M3×2(R). Compute P13A, D2(5)A and (I3−3E31)A, and check that each is the result of the corresponding row operation.

exm-extend-basis-by-elimination.title: Extending to a basis by elimination

exm-gauss-jordan-3x4.html: Solve the following system over R by Gauss–Jordan elimination, naming each operation: 2x2−2x3+x4=3,x1+x2+x3+x4=3,2x1+x2+3x3+x4=3.

exm-independence-by-rank.title: Testing independence
exm-independence-by-rank.html: Decide whether v1=(1,2,0,1), v2=(2,4,1,1), v3=(0,0,1,−1) are linearly independent in R4. If not, find a linear relation.

exm-interpolation-cubic.title: A cubic through four points
exm-interpolation-cubic.html: Find the polynomial p∈Q[x]≤3 whose graph passes through (−1,2), (0,1), (1,2) and (2,11).

exm-intersection-by-elimination.title: A basis of an intersection
exm-intersection-by-elimination.html: For U and W as in @exm-sum-by-elimination, find a basis of U∩W, and check the Dimension Formula for Sums.

exm-inverse-3x3.title: A 3 \times 3 inverse

exm-inverse-3x3.html: Find the inverse of A=(121253133)∈M3(R), or show that it does not exist.

exm-inverse-fails-zero-row.title: When the algorithm stops
exm-inverse-fails-zero-row.html: Decide whether A=(123257134)∈M3(R) is invertible.

exm-lights-out-3x3.title: Every pattern of the 3 × 3 puzzle is solvable
exm-lights-out-3x3.title_html: Every pattern of the 3 × 3 puzzle is solvable

exm-lights-out-center.title: Switching off the center
exm-lights-out-center.html: Only the center light is on. Which buttons should be pressed?

exm-lu-by-elimination.title: An LU factorization from elimination
exm-lu-by-elimination.html: Let A=(21−145−1−282)∈M3(Q). Reduce A to upper triangular form using only operations “subtract a multiple of a higher row from a lower row”, and record each multiplier. Compare the result with the matrix U of the previous subsection.

exm-lu-solve.title: Two right-hand sides, one factorization
exm-lu-solve.html: Let A=(21−145−1−282) with the factorization A=LU of @exm-lu-by-elimination. Solve Ax=b for b=(−1−3−6)andb′=(37−2).

exm-product-of-elementary-matrices.title: Factoring into elementary matrices
exm-product-of-elementary-matrices.html: Write A=(2153)∈M2(R) as a product of elementary matrices, and read off A−1.

exm-solution-set-p-plus-span.title: Particular plus homogeneous
exm-solution-set-p-plus-span.html: Solve x1+2x2−x3=4, x2+x3=1 over R, and write the solution set in the form p+span(h).

exm-span-membership-by-system.title: Span membership as a system
exm-span-membership-by-system.html: In R3, let v1=(1,2,3) and v2=(0,1,2). Decide whether (1,4,7) and (1,4,8) lie in span(v1,v2).

exm-sum-by-elimination.title: A basis of a sum
exm-sum-by-elimination.html: Let U=span(u1,u2) and W=span(w1,w2) in R4, where u1=(1,0,1,2),u2=(0,1,1,1),w1=(1,1,0,1),w2=(1,3,0,1). Find a basis and the dimension of U+W.

exm-system-over-f2-two-solutions.title: Exactly two solutions over \nF_2
exm-system-over-f2-two-solutions.title_html: Exactly two solutions over F2
exm-system-over-f2-two-solutions.html: Find all solutions of the system x+y+z=1, y+z=0 over F2. Then compare with the same system over R.

exm-system-with-parameter.title: A system with a parameter
exm-system-with-parameter.html: For which k∈R does the system x+ky=1, kx+y=1 have no solution, exactly one solution, or infinitely many? Find the solutions when they exist.

exm-three-kinds-of-solution-sets.title: None, one, or a whole line
exm-three-kinds-of-solution-sets.title_html: None, one, or a whole line
exm-three-kinds-of-solution-sets.html:
Find the solution set of each system over R, and describe it in the row picture.

  1. x+2y=1, 2x+4y=5.
  2. 2x−y=1, x+y=5.
  3. x+2y=1, 2x+4y=2.

exm-traffic-network.title: Traffic in a town center
exm-traffic-network.html:
Four intersections are joined by one-way streets 1→2, 2→3, 3→4, 4→1 and 1→3, carrying unknown flows f1,…,f5 (cars per minute) in that order. From outside, 40 cars per minute enter at intersection 1 and 20 at intersection 2, while 35 leave at intersection 3 and 25 at intersection 4.

Find all flows that satisfy conservation. If street 4→1 is closed for repairs and flows cannot be negative, what is the largest flow the diagonal street 1→3 may have to carry?

exm-two-echelon-forms-same-rref.title: Two echelon forms, one reduced form
exm-two-echelon-forms-same-rref.title_html: Two echelon forms, one reduced form
exm-two-echelon-forms-same-rref.html:
Let A=(121324023627) over R.

  1. Reduce A to a row echelon form in two ways: first using row 1 as the first pivot row, then starting with R1↔R2.
  2. Continue both to reduced row echelon form.
  3. Read the column relations of A off the RREF.

exr-applications-a1.title: A1
exr-applications-a1.html:
1. State the polynomial interpolation theorem, including its hypotheses.
  2. True or false: there is a polynomial p∈R[x]≤1 with p(1)=2 and p(1)=3. Which hypothesis of the theorem fails?
  3. In balancing a chemical equation, what does it mean if the null space of the coefficient matrix has dimension 1? Dimension 2?
  4. Why is lights out modeled over F2 and not over R?
  5. A connected network has 6 vertices and 9 edges. What is the rank of its incidence matrix, and how many free parameters does the solution set of a consistent flow problem have?

exr-applications-b1.title: B1: Interpolating four points
exr-applications-b1.html: Find the polynomial p∈Q[x]≤3 with p(0)=−1, p(1)=1, p(2)=3 and p(3)=11. Justify that there is only one.

exr-applications-b2.title: B2: Balancing a redox reaction
exr-applications-b2.html: Potassium permanganate reacts with hydrochloric acid: aKMnO4+bHCl⟶cKCl+dMnCl2+eH2O+fCl2. Write the conservation equations for K, Mn, O, H and Cl, find all rational solutions, and hence the balanced equation with the smallest positive integer coefficients.

exr-applications-b3.title: B3: A ring road
exr-applications-b3.html:
Four intersections lie on a ring of one-way streets 1→2, 2→3, 3→4, 4→1, with flows f1,f2,f3,f4 in that order. From outside, 30 cars per minute enter at intersection 1 and 10 at intersection 3, while 15 leave at intersection 2 and 25 at intersection 4.

  1. Write down the incidence matrix N and the supply vector s, and explain without computation why the system Nf=s is consistent.
  2. Find all solutions.
  3. If all flows must be non-negative, what is the smallest possible flow on each street?

exr-applications-c1.title: C1: The 2 × 2 puzzle
exr-applications-c1.html:
Consider lights out on a 2×2 grid, where pressing a light toggles it and its two horizontal and vertical neighbors. Number the cells 1=(1,1), 2=(1,2), 3=(2,1), 4=(2,2).

  1. Write down the matrix A∈M4(F2) of the puzzle.
  2. Show that A2=I.
  3. Deduce that every pattern is solvable by exactly one set of presses, and find the presses that switch off the pattern with only light 1 on.

exr-applications-c2.title: C2: Interpolating values and slopes
exr-applications-c2.html:
For p=c0+c1x+c2x2+c3x3∈F[x]≤3, define its (formal) derivative p′=c1+2c2x+3c3x2.

  1. Prove that for every field F and all a,b,c,d∈F there is exactly one p∈F[x]≤3 with p(0)=a,p′(0)=b,p(1)=c,p′(1)=d.
  2. Find this p over Q for (a,b,c,d)=(0,1,1,0).

Hint: in (a), check that elimination never divides by an element that could be zero in some field.

exr-applications-c3.title: C3: Networks in several pieces
exr-applications-c3.html:
Let N∈Mm×k(R) be the incidence matrix of a network with m vertices. Say that vertices v and w are linked if they are joined by a sequence of vertices in which consecutive ones share an edge, in either direction (every vertex is linked to itself by the sequence of length zero).

  1. Show that “linked” is an equivalence relation. Its equivalence classes are called the components of the network; let c be their number.
  2. Prove that rankN=m−c.

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-a1.title: A1
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-a1.html:
1. Define an elementary matrix, and write down the 3×3 elementary matrix that performs R3→R3+7R1.
  2. State four of the conditions in @thm-invertible-tfae.
  3. True or false: the product of two elementary matrices is always an elementary matrix. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: if A∈M2×3(F), B∈M3×2(F) and AB=I2, then BA=I3. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: if A∈Mn(F) and Ax=ej has a solution for each j=1,…,n, then A is invertible. Justify your answer.
  6. Describe the method for computing the inverse of a square matrix, and how it detects a matrix that is not invertible.

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b1.title: B1: Inverses by row reduction
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b1.html:
For each matrix, find the inverse or show that it is not invertible.

  1. A=(102213418)∈M3(R).
  2. B=(12−101125−1)∈M3(R).

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b2.title: B2: A product of elementary matrices
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b2.title_html: B2: A product of elementary matrices
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b2.html:

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b3.title: B3: Invertible products
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-b3.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F), and suppose AB is invertible. Prove that A and B are both invertible.

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c1.title: C1: Triangular matrices
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c1.html:
Let U=(uij)∈Mn(F) be upper triangular (@def-upper-triangular).

  1. Prove that U is invertible if and only if uii≠0 for every i.
  2. Prove that if U is invertible, then U−1 is upper triangular.

Hint: for (a), use item (b) or item (f) of @thm-invertible-tfae; for (b), consider the systems Ux=ek.

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c2.title: C2: All right inverses
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c2.html:
Let A=(101011)∈M2×3(R).

  1. Find all B∈M3×2(R) with AB=I2.
  2. Show that there is no C∈M3×2(R) with CA=I3.

exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c3.title: C3: Nilpotent perturbations of the identity
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c3.title_html: C3: Nilpotent perturbations of the identity
exr-elementary-matrices-and-inverses-c3.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) and suppose Ak=0 for some integer k≥1.

  1. Prove that In+A is invertible, by using item (b) of @thm-invertible-tfae.
  2. Verify that (In+A)(In−A+A2−⋯+(−1)k−1Ak−1)=In, and deduce a formula for (In+A)−1.

exr-gaussian-elimination-a1.title: A1
exr-gaussian-elimination-a1.html:
1. List the three types of elementary row operation, including the conditions on the scalar and on the indices.
  2. Determine whether the following statement is true: “every matrix in row echelon form is in reduced row echelon form.” Justify your answer.
  3. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if the RREF of [A∣b] has a zero row, then Ax=b is inconsistent.” Justify your answer.
  4. Determine whether the following statement is true: “a homogeneous system of 3 equations in 5 unknowns over R has infinitely many solutions.” Justify your answer.
  5. Explain why swapping two columns of A in [A∣b] is not a safe step when solving Ax=b.

exr-gaussian-elimination-b1.title: B1: Reduce and solve
exr-gaussian-elimination-b1.html:
Reduce the augmented matrix of each system over R to reduced row echelon form, naming each operation. Hence decide whether the system is consistent, and if so, describe all solutions.

  1. x1+2x2−x3=1, 2x1+5x2+x3=4, x1+3x2+2x3=4.
  2. x1+x2+2x3=3, 2x1+3x2+5x3=7, x1+2x2+4x3=5.
  3. x1−x2+2x3+x4=2, 2x1−2x2+5x3+4x4=5, −x1+x2−x3+x4=−1.

exr-gaussian-elimination-b2.title: B2: A parameter
exr-gaussian-elimination-b2.html: For which k∈R is the system x+y−z=2,x+2y+z=3,x+y+(k2−5)z=k inconsistent, which give exactly one solution, and which give infinitely many? Justify your answer, and find the solutions when they exist.

exr-gaussian-elimination-b3.title: B3: Over \nF_3
exr-gaussian-elimination-b3.title_html: B3: Over F3
exr-gaussian-elimination-b3.html:
Solve each system over F3 by reducing to RREF, naming each operation, and list all solutions.

  1. x+2y+z=1, 2x+y+z=0, x+z=2.
  2. x+y+2z=1, 2x+z=2.

exr-gaussian-elimination-c1.title: C1: Why i \neq j?
exr-gaussian-elimination-c1.title_html: C1: Why i≠j?
exr-gaussian-elimination-c1.html:
Consider the move “Ri→Ri+cRi”, which the definition does not allow.

  1. Show that for c=−1 this move is not reversible: give a matrix on which its effect cannot be undone by any sequence of elementary row operations and moves of this kind, and a system whose solution set it changes.
  2. Show that for c≠−1 the move is an elementary row operation of another type. Explain why the condition i≠j in type (3) therefore loses nothing.

exr-gaussian-elimination-c2.title: C2: The cost of elimination
exr-gaussian-elimination-c2.html:
Let A∈Mn(F) and b∈Fn, and suppose that Gauss–Jordan elimination on [A∣b] finds, for each l=1,…,n, a non-zero entry in position (l,l) and so never swaps. Count as one operation each multiplication or division of two scalars, under these conventions: scaling row l costs one division for each entry in columns l+1,…,n+1 (the pivot is simply set to 1), and each replacement Rg→Rg−cRl costs one multiplication for each entry in columns l+1,…,n+1 (the entry in column l is simply set to 0).

  1. Show that processing column l costs at most n(n+1−l) operations.
  2. Hence show that the whole elimination costs at most 12(n3+n2) operations.
  3. Roughly how many times more work is a system of 2n equations than one of n equations, for large n?

exr-gaussian-elimination-c3.title: C3: Solvable for every right-hand side
exr-gaussian-elimination-c3.title_html: C3: Solvable for every right-hand side
exr-gaussian-elimination-c3.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F), and suppose that Ax=b is consistent for every b∈Fm. Prove that m≤n.

Hint: suppose m>n, reduce A to its RREF R, and run the operations backwards on [R∣em].

exr-linear-systems-a1.title: A1
exr-linear-systems-a1.html:
1. Define what it means for a linear system Ax=b over F to be consistent, and what its augmented matrix is. What is the size of the augmented matrix of a system of m equations in n unknowns?
  2. Determine whether the following statement is true: “the solution set of Ax=b is a subspace of Fn.” Justify your answer.
  3. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if Ax=b has two different solutions, then Ax=0 has a non-trivial solution.” Justify your answer.
  4. Let A∈M3×5(R). In which spaces do the unknown vector x and the right-hand side b of Ax=b live?
  5. Name the theorem that turns “is b in the span of a1,…,an?” into a question about a linear system, and state which system.

exr-linear-systems-b1.title: B1: Three views
exr-linear-systems-b1.html:
1. Write the system x1−x2+2x3=3, 2x1+x3=1 over R in the matrix picture and in the column picture, and give its augmented matrix.
  2. Write out, as a list of equations, the system with augmented matrix [1400123−15] over R. How many equations and unknowns does it have? Hence decide whether it is consistent.

exr-linear-systems-b2.title: B2: In the span or not?
exr-linear-systems-b2.title_html: B2: In the span or not?
exr-linear-systems-b2.html:
Determine whether the vector b lies in the span of the given vectors. Justify your answer, and when it does, write b as a linear combination of them.

  1. b=(2,1,4) and (1,0,1),(0,1,2) in R3.
  2. b=(1,1,1) and (1,2,0),(2,4,1) in R3.
  3. b=(1,1,0) and (1,0,1),(0,1,1) in F23. Is the answer the same in R3?

exr-linear-systems-b3.title: B3: Solve and describe
exr-linear-systems-b3.html:
Solve each system over R by substitution, and write its solution set in the form p+span(…). Check that your p is a solution and that your spanning vectors solve the associated homogeneous system.

  1. x1+x2+x3=2, x2−x3=1.
  2. x1−2x2+x3−x4=1, x3+2x4=3.

exr-linear-systems-c1.title: C1: How many solutions?
exr-linear-systems-c1.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) and b∈Fm, and let N be the solution set of Ax=0.

  1. Suppose F is infinite. Prove that Ax=b has either no solution, exactly one solution, or infinitely many solutions.
  2. Suppose F is finite. Prove that Ax=b has either no solution or exactly |N| solutions.
  3. Give a system over F3 with exactly three solutions.

Hint: for (a), if N contains a non-zero vector h, look at its multiples.

exr-linear-systems-c2.title: C2: The right-hand sides that work
exr-linear-systems-c2.title_html: C2: The right-hand sides that work
exr-linear-systems-c2.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) have columns a1,…,an.

  1. Prove that the set C={b∈Fm:Ax=b is consistent} is a subspace of Fm.
  2. Deduce that if n<m, then there is some b∈Fm for which Ax=b is inconsistent.
  3. For A=(122401) over R, find one such b.

exr-lu-factorization-a1.title: A1
exr-lu-factorization-a1.html:
1. Define an LU factorization of a matrix A∈Mn(F), and a PLU factorization.
  2. True or false: every invertible matrix has an LU factorization. Justify your answer.
  3. Suppose A=LU. In which order are the two triangular systems solved to find a solution of Ax=b, and what is each one?
  4. True or false: the product of two unit lower triangular n×n matrices is unit lower triangular. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: the zero matrix in M2(F) has more than one LU factorization. Justify your answer.
  6. What is the inverse of a permutation matrix P?

exr-lu-factorization-b1.title: B1: An LU factorization
exr-lu-factorization-b1.html: Find the LU factorization of A=(120−3−7426−3)∈M3(Q) by elimination without row swaps. Hence show that A is invertible.

exr-lu-factorization-b2.title: B2: Two systems, one factorization
exr-lu-factorization-b2.html: With A=LU as in @exr-lu-factorization-b1, solve Ax=b for b=(3,−6,5) and for b=(0,1,−2), using only forward and back substitution.

exr-lu-factorization-b3.title: B3: A PLU factorization
exr-lu-factorization-b3.html:
Let A=(012111231)∈M3(Q).

  1. Explain why A has no LU factorization.
  2. Find a PLU factorization of A.
  3. Hence solve Ax=(0,2,7).

exr-lu-factorization-c1.title: C1: Leading principal submatrices
exr-lu-factorization-c1.html:
For A∈Mn(F) and 1≤k≤n, the leading principal submatrix Ak∈Mk(F) is the top-left k×k corner of A, with entries aij for i,j≤k.

  1. Let L be lower triangular and U upper triangular in Mn(F). Show that (LU)k=LkUk for every k.
  2. Deduce that if A has an LU factorization A=LU with U invertible, then every leading principal submatrix A1,…,An is invertible.
  3. Prove the converse: if A1,…,An are all invertible, then A has an LU factorization with U invertible.

Hint for (c): induction on n. Write A with An−1 in its top-left corner, a column b, a row cT and a corner entry d, and look for L and U of the same shape.

exr-lu-factorization-c2.title: C2: An LDLᵀ factorization
exr-lu-factorization-c2.html:
Let A=(4−48−45−118−1127)∈M3(R).

  1. Find the LU factorization of A, show that A is invertible, and write A=LDLT.
  2. Deduce that xTAx>0 for every non-zero x∈R3.

exr-lu-factorization-c3.title: C3: Counting matrices without an LU factorization
exr-lu-factorization-c3.title_html: C3: Counting matrices without an LU factorization
exr-lu-factorization-c3.html:
1. Let A=(abcd)∈M2(F). Prove that A has an LU factorization if and only if a≠0 or c=0.
  2. Let q be a prime. How many matrices in M2(Fq) have no LU factorization? List them for q=2.

exr-rank-a1.title: A1
exr-rank-a1.html:
1. Define col(A), row(A), nul(A) and rankA for A∈Mm×n(F), and say which space each subspace lives in.
  2. State the Rank–Nullity Theorem for matrices and the Rouché–Capelli Theorem.
  3. True or false: if R is the RREF of A, then col(R)=col(A). Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: there is a 4×6 real matrix with nullity 1. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: for every A∈Mm×n(F), rankA=rankAT. Justify your answer.
  6. Describe how to find a basis of U∩W for subspaces U,W⊆Fm given by bases.

exr-rank-b1.title: B1: The three subspaces of a 3 \times 5 matrix
exr-rank-b1.title_html: B1: The three subspaces of a 3×5 matrix
exr-rank-b1.html: Let A=(1−12032−2514−11−11−5)∈M3×5(R). Find bases of col(A), row(A) and nul(A). Hence verify rankA+nullityA=5.

exr-rank-b2.title: B2: Independence and extension in \nR^4
exr-rank-b2.title_html: B2: Independence and extension in R4
exr-rank-b2.html:
Let v1=(1,0,2,1), v2=(2,1,3,1), v3=(0,1,−1,−1) in R4.

  1. Determine whether (v1,v2,v3) is linearly independent. Justify your answer.
  2. Find a basis of span(v1,v2,v3), and extend it to a basis of R4 using standard basis vectors.

exr-rank-b3.title: B3: Sum and intersection in \nR^5
exr-rank-b3.title_html: B3: Sum and intersection in R5
exr-rank-b3.html: Let U=span(u1,u2,u3) and W=span(w1,w2) in R5, where u1=(1,1,0,0,1),u2=(0,1,1,0,0),u3=(1,0,0,1,0),w1=(1,2,2,1,2),w2=(0,0,1,1,1). Find dim⁡U, dim⁡W, a basis of U+W and a basis of U∩W. Hence verify @thm-dimension-formula-subspace-dim.

exr-rank-c1.title: C1: Rank of a sum
exr-rank-c1.html: Let A,B∈Mm×n(F). Prove that rank(A+B)≤rankA+rankB. Give an example where the inequality is strict.

exr-rank-c2.title: C2: Matrices of rank one
exr-rank-c2.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F). Prove that rankA=1 if and only if A=xyT for some non-zero x∈Fm and y∈Fn.

exr-rank-c3.title: C3: The matrix i + j
exr-rank-c3.title_html: C3: The matrix i+j
exr-rank-c3.html:
For n≥1, let An∈Mn(R) have entries aij=i+j. Prove that rankA1=1 and rankAn=2 for every n≥2. Hence find nullityAn.

Hint: write each row as a combination of two fixed row vectors.

exr-rank-c4.title: C4: Counting right-hand sides over a finite field
exr-rank-c4.title_html: C4: Counting right-hand sides over a finite field
exr-rank-c4.html:
Let F be a finite field with q elements, and let A∈Mm×n(F) have rank r.

  1. Prove that exactly qr vectors b∈Fm make Ax=b consistent.
  2. By counting the pairs (x,b)∈Fn×Fm with Ax=b in two ways, and using @thm-general-solution-structure but not @thm-rank-nullity-matrix, prove that nul(A) has exactly qn−r elements. Deduce nullityA=n−r: a counting proof of Rank–Nullity over a finite field.
  3. Over F2, let A=(110011101). How many b∈F23 give a consistent system, and how many solutions does each such system have?

exr-rref-uniqueness-a1.title: A1
exr-rref-uniqueness-a1.html:
1. State the uniqueness theorem for the reduced row echelon form.
  2. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if A and B are row equivalent, then the columns of A and the columns of B span the same subspace.” Justify your answer.
  3. Determine whether the following statement is true: “if A and B are row equivalent and a3=a1−a2 for the columns of A, then b3=b1−b2 for the columns of B.” Justify your answer.
  4. Determine whether the following statement is true: “any two row echelon forms of the same matrix have the same number of zero rows.” Justify your answer.
  5. In the RREF of a matrix, what do the entries of a non-pivot column tell you about the original matrix?

exr-rref-uniqueness-b1.title: B1: Column relations
exr-rref-uniqueness-b1.html: Let A=(1−10212−21701−1151) over R. Find the RREF of A, naming each operation. Hence find the pivot columns of A, and express each non-pivot column of A as a linear combination of the pivot columns before it. Check your answer on the columns of A.

exr-rref-uniqueness-b2.title: B2: Row equivalence via the RREF
exr-rref-uniqueness-b2.title_html: B2: Row equivalence via the RREF
exr-rref-uniqueness-b2.html: Prove that two matrices A,B∈Mm×n(F) are row equivalent if and only if they have the same RREF.

exr-rref-uniqueness-b3.title: B3: Row equivalent or not?
exr-rref-uniqueness-b3.html:
Determine whether the matrices in each pair are row equivalent over R. Justify your answer.

  1. P=(123257) and Q=(112347).
  2. P=(111123012) and Q=(10−1012112).

exr-rref-uniqueness-c1.title: C1: Counting reduced forms
exr-rref-uniqueness-c1.html:
1. List, by pivot columns, all 2×3 matrices over F2 in reduced row echelon form, and show that there are exactly 15 of them.
  2. Deduce that M2×3(F2), which has 64 elements, splits into exactly 15 classes of row equivalent matrices.
  3. Show that over a field with q elements there are exactly 2q2+2q+3 such matrices.

exr-rref-uniqueness-c2.title: C2: Deleting a column
exr-rref-uniqueness-c2.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) with n≥2, and let R be its RREF.

  1. Let A′ and R′ be obtained from A and R by deleting the last column. Prove that R′ is the RREF of A′.
  2. Show by an example that the corresponding statement for deleting the first column is false.

lem-elimination-matrices.title: Multiplier matrices
lem-elimination-matrices.html:
Let 1≤k≤n, and let v,v1,…,vm∈Fn be vectors such that the first k entries of v are zero and, for each j, the first j entries of vj are zero (m≤n). Then:

  1. Gk(v) is the product, in any order, of the elementary matrices I+viEik for i=k+1,…,n;
  2. Gk(v)Gk(−v)=Gk(−v)Gk(v)=I;
  3. G1(v1)G2(v2)⋯Gm(vm)=I+v1e1T+v2e2T+⋯+vmemT.

lem-factor-theorem-linear.title: Factor Theorem for a Linear Divisor
lem-factor-theorem-linear.title_html: Factor Theorem for a Linear Divisor
lem-factor-theorem-linear.html: Let p∈F[x] and c∈F. Then there is q∈F[x] such that p=(x−c)q+p(c). In particular, if c is a root of p, then p=(x−c)q.

lem-permutation-matrices.title: Permutation matrices
lem-permutation-matrices.html:
Let σ,τ∈Sn.

  1. PσPτ=Pσ∘τ. In particular a product of permutation matrices is a permutation matrix.
  2. Pσ is invertible and Pσ−1=PσT.
  3. If τ=(r s) is a transposition, then Pτ is the elementary matrix Prs that swaps rows r and s, and Pτ2=I.
  4. Let 1≤k<r<s≤n, let τ=(r s), and let v∈Fn have its first k entries zero. Then Pτv has its first k entries zero, and PτGk(v)Pτ=Gk(Pτv).

lem-root-bound.title: Root bound
lem-root-bound.html: Let n∈N, and let p∈F[x] be non-zero with deg⁡p≤n. Then p has at most n distinct roots in F.

lem-row-equivalent-same-null-space.title: Row equivalent matrices have the same homogeneous solutions
lem-row-equivalent-same-null-space.title_html: Row equivalent matrices have the same homogeneous solutions
lem-row-equivalent-same-null-space.html: Let A,B∈Mm×n(F) be row equivalent. Then for every x∈Fn, Ax=0 if and only if Bx=0.

lem-row-ops-act-on-columns.title: Row operations act column by column
lem-row-ops-act-on-columns.title_html: Row operations act column by column
lem-row-ops-act-on-columns.html: Let M=[M1∣M2]∈Mm×k(F) be split into its first k1 columns M1 and its remaining columns M2. If an elementary row operation turns M into M′=[M1′∣M2′] (split in the same place), then the same operation turns M1 into M1′ and M2 into M2′. In particular, an elementary row operation turns a zero column into a zero column.

lem-row-ops-preserve-column-relations.title: Row operations preserve column relations
lem-row-ops-preserve-column-relations.html:
Let A,B∈Mm×n(F) have columns a1,…,an and b1,…,bn, and suppose that Ax=0⇔Bx=0 for every x∈Fn. This holds, for instance, if A and B are row equivalent (@lem-row-equivalent-same-null-space). Then:

  1. for all x1,…,xn∈F: x1a1+⋯+xnan=0 if and only if x1b1+⋯+xnbn=0;
  2. for every index l and all scalars d1,…,dl−1: al=d1a1+⋯+dl−1al−1 if and only if bl=d1b1+⋯+dl−1bl−1;
  3. for every index l: al∈span(a1,…,al−1) if and only if bl∈span(b1,…,bl−1).

lem-rref-columns.title: Columns of a matrix in RREF
lem-rref-columns.title_html: Columns of a matrix in RREF
lem-rref-columns.html:
Let R∈Mm×n(F) be in reduced row echelon form, with entries ril, columns u1,…,un, and pivot columns j1<⋯<jr.

  1. For each i=1,…,r, the pivot column uji is ei.
  2. If l is not a pivot column, then ul=∑i:ji<lrilei=∑i:ji<lriluji.
  3. Column l is a pivot column if and only if ul∉span(u1,…,ul−1).

lem-square-rref-identity-or-zero-row.title: Square reduced matrices
lem-square-rref-identity-or-zero-row.html: Let R∈Mn(F) be in reduced row echelon form. Then either R=In, or the last row of R is zero.

lem-triangular-invertible.title: Invertibility of a triangular matrix
lem-triangular-invertible.html: An upper triangular matrix U∈Mn(F) is invertible if and only if every diagonal entry u11,…,unn is non-zero.

lem-unit-lower-triangular-closed.title: Unit lower triangular matrices are closed
lem-unit-lower-triangular-closed.title_html: Unit lower triangular matrices are closed
lem-unit-lower-triangular-closed.html:
Let L,L′∈Mn(F) be unit lower triangular. Then:

  1. LL′ is unit lower triangular;
  2. L is invertible, and L−1 is unit lower triangular.

prp-incidence-rank-connected.title: Rank of an incidence matrix
prp-incidence-rank-connected.html: Let N∈Mm×k(R) be the incidence matrix of a connected network with m vertices. Then rankN=m−1.

prp-sum-intersection-by-elimination.title: Sum and intersection by elimination
prp-sum-intersection-by-elimination.html:
Let U,W⊆Fm be subspaces with bases (u1,…,uk) and (w1,…,wl), and let M=(u1⋯ukw1⋯wl)∈Mm×(k+l)(F). Then:

  1. the pivot columns of M form a basis of U+W;
  2. for x=(x1,…,xk+l)∈Fk+l write ux:=x1u1+⋯+xkuk, the combination of the u’s with the first k entries of x as coefficients. If (n1,…,nd) is a basis of nul(M), then (un1,…,und) is a basis of U∩W.

In particular dim⁡(U+W)=rankM and dim⁡(U∩W)=nullityM.

thm-basis-column-space.title: Pivot columns form a basis of the column space
thm-basis-column-space.title_html: Pivot columns form a basis of the column space
thm-basis-column-space.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) have pivot columns j1<⋯<jr, and let R=(rkj) be its RREF. Then:

  1. the pivot columns of A, (aj1,…,ajr), form a basis of col(A);
  2. if column j is free and t pivot columns lie to its left, then aj=r1jaj1+⋯+rtjajt;
  3. the pivot columns of A are exactly the vectors kept when (a1,…,an) is sifted as in @thm-sift.

thm-basis-null-space.title: Basis of the null space
thm-basis-null-space.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) have RREF R=(rkj) with pivot columns j1<⋯<jr. For each free column f, define sf∈Fn by (sf)f=1,(sf)f′=0 for every other free f′,(sf)jk=−rkf for k=1,…,r. Then the vectors sf, one for each free column f, form a basis of nul(A). In particular nullityA=n−r, the number of free columns.

thm-basis-row-space.title: Basis of the row space
thm-basis-row-space.html: The non-zero rows of the RREF R of A form a basis of row(A).

thm-consistent-iff-column-span.title: Consistency and the span of the columns
thm-consistent-iff-column-span.title_html: Consistency and the span of the columns
thm-consistent-iff-column-span.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) have columns a1,…,an∈Fm, and let b∈Fm. Then the system Ax=b is consistent if and only if b∈span(a1,…,an). More precisely, s=(s1,…,sn) is a solution exactly when b=s1a1+⋯+snan.

thm-elementary-invertible.title: Elementary matrices are invertible
thm-elementary-invertible.html: Every elementary matrix is invertible, and its inverse is an elementary matrix of the same kind: Pij−1=Pij,Di(c)−1=Di(c−1),(Im+cEij)−1=Im−cEij(i≠j).

thm-general-solution-structure.title: Structure of the solution set
thm-general-solution-structure.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) and b∈Fm, let N be the solution set of Ax=0, and suppose p∈Fn is one solution of Ax=b. Then the solution set of Ax=b is p+N={p+h:h∈N}.

thm-homogeneous-solutions-subspace.title: Homogeneous solutions form a subspace
thm-homogeneous-solutions-subspace.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F). The solution set N={x∈Fn:Ax=0} of the homogeneous system Ax=0 is a subspace of Fn.

thm-independence-spanning-by-rank.title: Independence and spanning by rank
thm-independence-spanning-by-rank.html:
Let v1,…,vk∈Fm, and let A=(v1⋯vk)∈Mm×k(F). Then:

  1. (v1,…,vk) is linearly independent if and only if rankA=k, that is, every column is a pivot column;
  2. (v1,…,vk) spans Fm if and only if rankA=m, that is, every row of the RREF has a pivot;
  3. (v1,…,vk) is a basis of Fm if and only if k=m=rankA.

thm-interpolation-unique.title: Polynomial interpolation
thm-interpolation-unique.html: Let x0,x1,…,xn∈F be distinct, and let y0,y1,…,yn∈F be arbitrary. Then there is exactly one polynomial p∈F[x]≤n with p(xi)=yi for i=0,1,…,n.

thm-inverse-by-row-reduction.title: Inverse by row reduction
thm-inverse-by-row-reduction.html: Let A∈Mn(F), and let [R∣C] be the reduced row echelon form of [A∣In], with R,C∈Mn(F). Then R is the reduced row echelon form of A. Consequently, A is invertible if and only if R=In, and in that case A−1=C.

thm-invertible-tfae.title: Invertible Matrix Theorem
thm-invertible-tfae.html:
Let A∈Mn(F), with columns a1,…,an∈Fn. The following are equivalent.

  1. A is invertible.
  2. The homogeneous system Ax=0 has only the trivial solution x=0.
  3. The reduced row echelon form of A is In.
  4. A is a product of elementary matrices.
  5. For every b∈Fn, the system Ax=b has a solution.
  6. The columns (a1,…,an) are linearly independent.
  7. The columns (a1,…,an) span Fn.
  8. The columns (a1,…,an) form a basis of Fn.

thm-ldlt.title: LDLᵀ factorization
thm-ldlt.html: Let A∈Mn(F) be symmetric and invertible, and suppose A=LU is an LU factorization. Then the diagonal entries u11,…,unn of U are non-zero, and with D=diag(u11,…,unn), U=DLTandA=LDLT.

thm-lu-exists-without-swaps.title: LU from elimination
thm-lu-exists-without-swaps.html: Let A∈Mn(F), and suppose elimination without row swaps succeeds on A, with multipliers ℓik and result U. Let L be the unit lower triangular matrix whose (i,k)-entry is ℓik for every i>k. Then U is upper triangular and A=LU. In particular A has an LU factorization.

thm-lu-unique.title: Uniqueness of the LU factorization
thm-lu-unique.html: Let A∈Mn(F) be invertible. If A=L1U1 and A=L2U2 are LU factorizations, then L1=L2 and U1=U2.

thm-one-sided-inverse.title: One-sided inverses of square matrices
thm-one-sided-inverse.html: Let A,B∈Mn(F). If AB=In, then BA=In. Hence A and B are both invertible, B=A−1 and A=B−1.

thm-plu-exists.title: Existence of a PLU factorization
thm-plu-exists.html: Every A∈Mn(F) has a PLU factorization.

thm-rank-nullity-matrix.title: Rank–Nullity for Matrices
thm-rank-nullity-matrix.html: For every A∈Mm×n(F), rankA+nullityA=n, the number of columns of A.

thm-rank-product-inequality.title: Rank of a product
thm-rank-product-inequality.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) and B∈Mn×p(F). Then rank(AB)≤min(rankA,rankB). Moreover, if P∈Mm(F) and Q∈Mn(F) are invertible, then rank(PA)=rankA=rank(AQ).

thm-reading-rref.title: Reading solutions from the RREF
thm-reading-rref.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) and b∈Fm, and suppose [A∣b] is row equivalent to a matrix [R∣c] in reduced row echelon form. Let ril be the entries of R and c=(c1,…,cm).

  1. Ax=b is inconsistent if and only if the last column, column n+1, is a pivot column of [R∣c], that is, some row of [R∣c] is (0 ⋯ 0∣1).
  2. Suppose there is no pivot in the last column. Let j1<⋯<jr be the pivot columns. Then for every choice of scalars tl∈F, one for each free variable xl, there is exactly one solution with xl=tl for all free l, namely the one with xji=ci−∑l freeriltl(i=1,…,r). In particular, setting every free variable to 0 gives the solution p with pji=ci and all other entries 0.
  3. A consistent system Ax=b has exactly one solution if and only if it has no free variables, that is, each of the columns 1,…,n is a pivot column.

thm-rouche-capelli.title: Rouché–Capelli Theorem
thm-rouche-capelli.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F), b∈Fm, and let [A∣b]∈Mm×(n+1)(F) be the augmented matrix.

  1. The system Ax=b is consistent if and only if rankA=rank[A∣b].
  2. Suppose it is consistent, let p be one solution, let r=rankA, and let s1,…,sn−r be a basis of nul(A). Then every solution can be written as x=p+t1s1+⋯+tn−rsn−r for exactly one choice of (t1,…,tn−r)∈Fn−r. In words: the solutions form an (n−r)-parameter family.
  3. If moreover F is a finite field with q elements (for instance Fp, with q=p), a consistent system has exactly qn−rankA solutions.

thm-row-equivalent-iff-invertible-multip.title: Row equivalence is left multiplication by an invertible matrix
thm-row-equivalent-iff-invertible-multip.title_html: Row equivalence is left multiplication by an invertible matrix
thm-row-equivalent-iff-invertible-multip.html: Let A,B∈Mm×n(F). Then A is row equivalent to B (that is, B can be reached from A by row operations) if and only if B=EA for some invertible E∈Mm(F).

thm-row-op-is-left-multiplication.title: Row operations are left multiplications
thm-row-op-is-left-multiplication.html: Let ρ be an elementary row operation on matrices with m rows, and let E=ρ(Im) be the corresponding elementary matrix. Then for every n≥1 and every A∈Mm×n(F), ρ(A)=EA.

thm-row-ops-preserve-solutions.title: Row operations preserve solutions
thm-row-ops-preserve-solutions.html:
Let F be a field.

  1. (Reversibility) If an elementary row operation turns M into M′, then an elementary row operation of the same type turns M′ back into M.
  2. Row equivalence is an equivalence relation on Mm×k(F).
  3. If [A∣b] and [A′∣b′] in Mm×(n+1)(F) are row equivalent, then the systems Ax=b and A′x=b′ have the same solution set.

thm-row-ops-row-space.title: Row operations and the three spaces
thm-row-ops-row-space.title_html: Row operations and the three spaces
thm-row-ops-row-space.html:
Let A,B∈Mm×n(F) be row equivalent. Then:

  1. row(B)=row(A);
  2. nul(B)=nul(A). Equivalently, writing b1,…,bn for the columns of B: for all c1,…,cn∈F, the columns of A satisfy c1a1+⋯+cnan=0 if and only if the columns of B satisfy c1b1+⋯+cnbn=0;
  3. but col(B) and col(A) need not be equal.

thm-row-rank-equals-column-rank.title: Row rank equals column rank
thm-row-rank-equals-column-rank.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F), and let r be the number of pivots of its RREF. Then dim⁡row(A)=dim⁡col(A)=r. Consequently rankA=rankAT.

thm-rref-exists.title: Existence of the reduced row echelon form
thm-rref-exists.title_html: Existence of the reduced row echelon form
thm-rref-exists.html: Let F be a field. Every matrix M∈Mm×k(F) is row equivalent to a matrix in reduced row echelon form.

thm-rref-unique.title: Uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form
thm-rref-unique.title_html: Uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form
thm-rref-unique.html:
Let R,R′∈Mm×n(F) be in reduced row echelon form, and suppose that Rx=0⇔R′x=0 for every x∈Fn. Then R=R′.

Consequently, every matrix A∈Mm×n(F) is row equivalent to exactly one matrix in reduced row echelon form, called the RREF of A.
